patients.summary: Construction supervisor with chronic low back pain on pain-clinic oxycodone, severe daily alcohol use and alcoholic liver disease with suspected cirrhosis, who joined in 2023. In 2026 he has acetaminophen toxicity, an opioid overdose and a hematemesis admission complicated by delirium tremens.

documents.title: New patient scheduling call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Ryan phoned wanting to transfer his primary care here; his old office is closing its internal medicine side. Membership paperwork emailed. New patient visit set for 9/12 at 7:40 am (he wants the earliest slot, on site by 9 most days). Signed release on file for prior PCP records; request sent today. He says a pain management office writes his pain medicine and he wants to keep them for that.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 50 y/o man, here to set up care. Supervises crews for a commercial builder, on his feet and climbing most of the day.

Back: low back pain for close to ten years, worse after long days on site, no leg weakness, no bowel or bladder change. Brother has the same problem. A pain management office has prescribed oxycodone 5 mg, one or two tabs up to every 6 hours as needed, for years; he gets it filled monthly and says he uses 2-4 tabs most days. He wants that to stay with them.

Alcohol: open about it. A pint of vodka most nights, more on weekends, for many years. Was told at his last office that his liver was damaged from drinking and that it might be cirrhosis; never saw a liver specialist. Has not had withdrawal seizures that he knows of. Not interested in a program right now: "I know, I know." Wife would like him to cut back.

Other: omeprazole 20 mg daily, started by the old office to protect the stomach. Appendix out at 11. Quit cigarettes in 2018 after about 20 pack-years. No drug allergies. Father drank heavily and had high blood pressure; mother has arthritis.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, no jaundice, no asterixis. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no palpable liver edge, no fluid wave. Paraspinal tenderness low lumbar, straight leg raise negative both sides, strength and reflexes symmetric. No spider angiomas noted, no edema.

AUDIT-C 12. PHQ-2 0. Pain 5/10.

A/P
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe by history. Spent a good part of the visit on this. Recommended cutting down with a goal of stopping; offered counseling referral and medication options, declined for now. Will keep asking.
2. Alcoholic liver disease, cirrhosis suspected, not confirmed. CMP, CBC, PT/INR, GGT today. RUQ ultrasound. Hep A/B status; vaccinate if not immune.
3. Chronic low back pain on pain clinic oxycodone. Not adding anything. Reviewed mixing opioid with alcohol.
4. Omeprazole continued, refills here.
5. Health maintenance: eligible for lung screening (20 pk-yr, quit within 15 yrs) - LDCT ordered. FIT kit given. Hep C and HIV screens with labs. Flu, COVID and pneumococcal shots next month at a nurse visit along with hepatitis vaccines if needed.
Follow up in 3 months.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn, your labs are back. Your liver tests show the pattern we see with alcohol: the AST is higher than the ALT and the GGT is well up. Bilirubin is a touch high and albumin a touch low, and your platelets are mildly low. Together these fit the liver damage you were told about, and they are one more reason to cut back. Kidneys and blood counts otherwise fine. Hepatitis C, HIV and hepatitis B screens are all negative. You are not immune to hepatitis B, so we will start that series and hepatitis A when you come in for your shots. Ultrasound is scheduled for the 26th.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 14 pages from prior primary care office covering 2019-2023. Problem list: chronic low back pain, alcohol use disorder, alcoholic liver disease (cirrhosis suspected). Medications: omeprazole 20 mg daily; oxycodone per pain management. NKDA. Appendectomy in childhood. Notes repeatedly document advice to reduce alcohol. No liver imaging in the packet. Scanned and routed to PCP.

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound abdomen, right upper quadrant.
INDICATION: Alcohol use, suspected cirrhosis.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: The liver is coarsened and diffusely echogenic with a subtly nodular surface contour. No focal hepatic lesion. Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. No ascites. Gallbladder is normally distended without stones, wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct measures 4 mm. No intrahepatic ductal dilatation. Right kidney unremarkable. Spleen is normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Coarsened, echogenic liver with subtly nodular contour, suggestive of cirrhosis. No focal liver lesion. No ascites.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Your liver ultrasound shows a liver that looks scarred, the kind of change that suggests cirrhosis. No mass and no fluid in the belly, and the blood flow to the liver is normal. This doesn't change what matters most, which is the alcohol. Happy to talk it through by phone or at your next visit.

Patient reply 9/28: ok got it. see you in december

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work for shots ordered by PCP. Screening questions negative, no allergies. Given: flu (L deltoid), COVID updated (R deltoid), PCV20 (L deltoid, 1 inch apart), hep A #1 (R deltoid), hep B #1 (R deltoid, separate site). VIS sheets given. Waited 15 min without issue. Hep B #2 due in 1 month; hep A #2 and hep B #3 in 6 months, reminders set.

EXAM: Low-dose CT chest without contrast, lung cancer screening, baseline.
INDICATION: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2018.
FINDINGS: Lungs are clear without nodules, consolidation or emphysema. Airways patent. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal; no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen without acute finding. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Hep B #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep B #2 given L deltoid, tolerated. No reaction to last month's shots per pt. LDCT and FIT both negative, he had seen the messages. Next: hep A #2 + hep B #3 in April.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 month f/u. Back is worse with the cold and a big job wrapping up before the holidays. Still on pain clinic oxycodone, same amount. Drinking unchanged by his account; tried a dry week in November and made it 3 days. No shakes in the mornings he'll admit to. Appetite ok, no abdominal swelling, no yellowing, no black stools.

Exam: VS as charted. No icterus. Abdomen soft, no ascites. Lumbar paraspinal tightness, neuro intact in legs.

AUDIT-C 12. Pain 6/10.

A/P
AUD - again offered referral to counseling and a medication; again declines. Talked about not stopping cold turkey on his own given how much he drinks, call us first.
ALD w/ suspected cirrhosis - imaging as above; labs again in spring.
Low back pain - heat, stretching; pain clinic continues meds.
Hep vaccines on track. RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Chronic care follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for back/liver/alcohol check. Season starting up at work. Back about the same, pain clinic visit last month, nothing changed there. Still a pint most days. Denies jaundice, swelling, confusion, vomiting blood or black stool. Sleeps poorly.

Exam: VS as charted, weight steady. Not jaundiced. Abd soft, no shifting dullness. No edema. Lumbar exam unchanged.

Assessment / plan:
- Alcohol use disorder: brief intervention again. Wife came up in conversation, she is worried. He is "thinking about it." Door left open for a counseling referral.
- Alcoholic liver disease, cirrhosis suspected: labs today.
- Chronic LBP: as before.
- Hep A #2 / hep B #3 next month.
Back in about 4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver numbers look about the same as in September. Same message as before, honestly: the best thing for these numbers is less alcohol. Let me know when you're ready and we'll make a plan together.

documents.title: Hep A #2, hep B #3
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Final doses: hep A #2 R deltoid, hep B #3 L deltoid. No problems. Both series complete, updated in record.

documents.title: Missed yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Sorry about yesterday, concrete pour got moved up and I was on site at 6. Can we do something in July early morning?

Front desk reply 6/20: Rebooked for Tuesday 7/9 at 7:40.

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled f/u. Summer is better for his back. Prescription monitoring report reviewed today: oxycodone 5 mg from the pain management prescriber, one fill every month, no other controlled fills. Says he's down to "most of a pint" on weeknights. No new GI symptoms.

Exam: well appearing, no jaundice, abdomen benign, ambulates normally.

A/P: AUD with liver disease - acknowledged effort, still well above any safe amount; repeated offer of help. LBP stable. Physical in October with labs, flu and the first shingles shot.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical, 51 y/o.

Interval: no ED visits or hospital stays. Back unchanged; pain management still prescribing oxycodone 5 mg as needed. Omeprazole daily. Still drinking daily, roughly a pint; his wife has been after him about it.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, jaundice, hematemesis, melena, leg swelling or confusion. Sleep fragmented. Mood ok.

PMH: chronic LBP, AUD, alcoholic liver disease (cirrhosis suspected on US 9/2023). Appendectomy age 11. Former smoker, quit 2018. NKDA.

Exam: VS as charted. Anicteric. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites, no palpable spleen. No edema. Skin: no jaundice. Neuro: no tremor, gait normal.

PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 12.

A/P
- Health maintenance: flu, COVID, Shingrix #1 today (#2 in 2-6 mo). LDCT due, ordered. FIT kit handed over. Lipids and A1c with today's draw. Hep A/B series done, PCV20 done.
- Alcohol use disorder / liver: same counseling; he would rather do it on his own. Labs today.
- LBP: no change.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol and sugar are fine. Liver tests are in the same range as before, not better and not worse. Lung CT is set for November 7.

FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodule. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. No emphysematous change. Normal heart size. No adenopathy. Limited upper abdominal images without acute abnormality. Osseous structures unremarkable.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chronic f/u. Long winter, back has been stiff, worse first thing in the morning. Pain clinic oxycodone unchanged. Alcohol: same, pint most nights. No GI bleeding, no yellow eyes, no belly swelling, no confusion per him (wife not here).

Exam: VS as charted. No scleral icterus. Abdomen soft, no ascites appreciated. Lumbar ROM limited by pain, neuro normal.

A/P
1. AUD - I was more direct today about where this goes with his liver. He listened. Still declining a referral or medication.
2. ALD, suspected cirrhosis - labs.
3. Chronic LBP - walking, core stretching sheet given; pain clinic manages medication.
F/u 3-4 months, video ok.

documents.title: March labs

Back better with warm weather, pain 4/10. Same oxycodone from pain management. Drinking: "a little less, maybe." No GI symptoms.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 52 y/o man.

Since last fall: no ER or hospital. Back pain steady, pain clinic still writing oxycodone 5 mg prn. Omeprazole daily. Alcohol unchanged overall per him; wife had told our front desk she is worried.

ROS negative for jaundice, abdominal swelling, GI bleeding, chest pain, shortness of breath, falls.

Exam: VS as charted, weight stable. Anicteric. Neck no masses. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, liver not palpable, no ascites. Ext without edema. No tremor. Skin no rashes.

AUDIT-C 12. PHQ-9 2.

A/P
Prevention: flu, updated COVID and Tdap (no tetanus record in his old chart, he can't recall one) today. LDCT and FIT again. Lipids, A1c in the draw.
AUD / alcoholic liver disease: advice repeated, he declines referral. Labs.
Low back pain: stable.
See him in early 2026.

events.reason: Nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain

documents.title: Emergency department note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 01/01/2026. Faxed to PCP 01/06/2026.

52M with alcohol use disorder, alcoholic liver disease (?cirrhosis), chronic back pain on oxycodone, presents with two days of nausea, emesis and RUQ abdominal pain. Has had a headache this past week and took more than the usual amount of OTC pain reliever, he describes it as "a few extra."

Meds: oxycodone 5-10 mg q6h prn, omeprazole 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: lethargic, oriented to person and place. Jaundiced skin, icteric sclerae. RUQ tenderness, no rebound, no guarding.

Labs: AST 2500, ALT 2300, T bili 5.2, INR 2.1. Acetaminophen level 30 mcg/mL (ref 10-20).

Impression: acetaminophen hepatotoxicity on background alcoholic liver disease.
Plan: N-acetylcysteine infusion started in ED. Admit to medicine. Poison center contacted.

documents.title: Glenn is in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
This is Glenn's wife on his account. He went to the ER yesterday with stomach pain and throwing up and they said his liver is bad from Tylenol he took for a headache. He's admitted and on an IV medicine. Just wanted you to know.

PCP reply 1/2: Thank you for letting me know. I'll ask the hospital for records. Please have him make an appointment with me within a week or so of getting home, and no Tylenol or anything with acetaminophen in it for now.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his New Year's Day ED visit and admission. ED note received 1/6; no discharge summary yet. By his account he was in about four days, got the IV antidote the whole time, and went home on the 5th once the numbers were coming down. He had a bad headache over Christmas week and took extra OTC acetaminophen on top of his usual drinking, didn't count the pills. Nausea gone, eating, no abdominal pain now. Says he hasn't had a drink since he got out but is vague.

Exam: VS as charted. Sclerae anicteric today. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites. Alert and oriented x3, no asterixis.

A/P
1. Acetaminophen toxicity, recovering. Repeat hepatic panel and INR today. No acetaminophen in any form - went through his medicine cabinet list with him, including combination cold products.
2. Alcohol use disorder with alcoholic liver disease. This was a scare for both of them. Offered referral again; he will think about it this week. AUDIT-C remains 12 for the past year.
3. Back pain - oxycodone through pain clinic, no change.
Portal me with how he's doing, recheck labs at next visit.

documents.title: Liver tests improving
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn, good news: your liver enzymes have come way down from the hospital (AST 74, ALT 168), bilirubin is 2.1 and clotting is 1.3. Still healing. Keep away from acetaminophen and alcohol and let's see you in a couple of months.

documents.title: ICU discharge summary (outside)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, critical care service. Admitted 03/08/2026, discharged 03/10/2026. Received by fax 03/24/2026.

Reason for admission: opioid overdose with hypoventilation.

Brief history: 52M with alcohol use disorder, alcoholic liver disease and acetaminophen toxicity in January 2026, on prescribed oxycodone for chronic back pain. Wife brought him to the ED after several hours of worsening drowsiness and slow, shallow breathing. He drinks regularly and denies other drug use.

On arrival: RR 8, BP 110/70, HR 55, SpO2 89% on room air. Somnolent, rousable to voice.
ABG: pH 7.28 / PaCO2 65 / PaO2 58 / HCO3 24 - acute respiratory acidosis.

Course: responded to IV naloxone in the ED with improved respiratory effort. Admitted to ICU for monitoring for recurrent sedation; no further naloxone needed after the first night. Breathing and mentation normal by day 2.

Discharge medications: omeprazole 20 mg daily; oxycodone 5-10 mg q6h prn (per outpatient prescriber); NEW naloxone 4 mg nasal spray, use for suspected overdose, call 911.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Back in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Glenn's wife again. Last night he got so sleepy I couldn't keep him awake and his breathing was really slow so I drove him in. They said it was the pain pills and gave him the reversal shot, he's in the ICU being watched but he's talking now.

PCP reply 3/9: I'm so glad you got him there. Please set up a visit for when he's home. I'll be in touch with the hospital team.

medications.sig: 1 spray in one nostril for suspected opioid overdose; call 911; may repeat in other nostril
medications.reason: Opioid overdose, prescribed at hospital discharge

documents.title: Post-ICU visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife after the ICU stay 3/8-3/10. No summary in yet; history from both of them. She found him very hard to wake and breathing slowly that evening and brought him in; he got naloxone in the ED and was watched in the ICU. He had taken his usual oxycodone and had been drinking. He says it was not on purpose, denies any thoughts of harming himself, and his wife agrees. He went home with a naloxone nasal spray; she has it in her purse and knows how to use it.

No breathing problems since. Back pain at baseline.

Exam: VS as charted. Alert, oriented, conversant. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No icterus today.

PHQ-9 4. AUDIT-C 12.

A/P
1. Opioid overdose with alcohol on board, 3/8. Naloxone kit at home, reviewed use with wife. Discussed that alcohol plus opioid is what makes this dangerous.
2. Alcohol use disorder - the conversation was more serious with his wife in the room. He still isn't ready for a program or a medication. I'll keep asking.
3. Recent acetaminophen toxicity - LFTs next visit.
4. Requesting ICU summary.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: ICU records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called hospital HIM for the 3/8-3/10 ICU stay; no summary sent yet. Re-faxed our request with signed release. Also asked again for the January discharge summary; told it may not have been dictated yet.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after a rough winter. ICU summary from March is in the chart (received 3/24). No further sedation episodes, naloxone still at home unused. No acetaminophen. Back to work full time. Drinking: says he cut down for a few weeks after March and is "back to about where I was."

No jaundice, no abdominal swelling, no GI bleeding.

Exam: VS as charted. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, no ascites. Lumbar tenderness as before.

A/P
- Acetaminophen toxicity: recovered; labs today should be back to his baseline. Closing the problem.
- Opioid overdose 3/2026: no recurrence. Closing as an active problem; kit at home.
- AUD / alcoholic liver disease with suspected cirrhosis: counseling, declines referral.
- LBP: unchanged.
Check in this summer.

documents.title: May labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your liver tests are back to where they were before January. The acetaminophen injury has healed. What's left is the alcohol-related damage we've been watching.

documents.title: Omeprazole refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Omeprazole 20 mg #90 refill sent. Seen 5/12.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sunday. His wife texted my phone at 7:50 that he had thrown up blood; video call at 8:10 with both of them at home, identity confirmed.

He has vomited blood this morning. Drank last night as usual.

On video: sitting at the kitchen table, speaking in full sentences, answering appropriately.

A/P: Hematemesis in a man with alcoholic liver disease and suspected cirrhosis. Needs emergency evaluation now. Told them to call 911 rather than drive; wife called while we were still on. Not to eat or drink anything. I phoned the ED charge nurse with his history (alcohol use disorder, suspected cirrhosis, acetaminophen toxicity 1/2026, opioid overdose 3/2026, oxycodone and omeprazole, NKDA).

reports.text:
EXAM: CT head without contrast.
INDICATION: Acute confusion and agitation.
FINDINGS: No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, mass effect or acute territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium intact. Visualized sinuses and mastoids clear.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (outside)
documents.author: internal medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 07/12/2026, discharged 07/21/2026. Received 07/24/2026.

Principal problem: hematemesis.
Hospital course complicated by: delirium tremens.

History: 53M with alcohol use disorder, alcoholic liver disease with suspected cirrhosis, prior critical care admissions this year (acetaminophen toxicity January, opioid overdose March), chronic back pain on oxycodone, sent in by his PCP after vomiting blood at home. Per wife he drinks a pint of vodka a day; last drink the day of admission.

Course: treated with IV acid suppression; no further hematemesis after admission. On hospital day 3 (07/14) he became increasingly agitated and confused, trying to get out of bed and saying there were spiders on the walls. T 38.6 C (101.5 F), BP 168/96, HR 122, RR 22. Diaphoretic, fine tremor, disoriented. Electrolytes within normal limits. Noncontrast head CT normal. Treated for delirium tremens with lorazepam and IV thiamine with ICU-level monitoring; delirium cleared over the following days and benzodiazepines were tapered off before discharge.

Discharge condition: alert and oriented, ambulating.
Discharge medications: omeprazole 20 mg daily; oxycodone 5-10 mg q6h prn (outpatient prescriber).
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 week. Strongly advised alcohol abstinence.

documents.title: He's home
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Glenn's wife. He came home yesterday. It was a really bad week, he was seeing things and didn't know where he was for a couple days. He's sleeping a lot but ok. They said to see you next week.

PCP reply 7/23: Thank you for the update, I'm relieved he's home. Yes, I want to see him soon, please call the office or reply here and we'll find a time that works. If he has any more bleeding, black stools, confusion or shaking, call 911.

documents.title: Scheduling outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt's cell to book post-hospital visit per PCP, discharge summary in chart 7/24. No answer, voicemail left with our number. Portal reminder sent.

documents.title: Omeprazole refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request omeprazole 20 mg #90. Sent per PCP. Still no post-hospital visit on the books; left another message on the portal asking him to call.
